title: MF vs. Sézary Syndrome vs. CD30+ Lymphoproliferative Disorders
subtitle: Key distinguishing features across the three major CTCL categories

values.ss: 60-70 years; older median age than MF
values.cd30: LyP: any age including children. pcALCL: 50-60 years

values.mf: Progressive patches → plaques → tumors; bathing-suit distribution; wrinkled cigarette-paper texture
values.ss: Erythroderma (≥80% BSA); exfoliative, pruritic; ectropion, leonine facies; palmoplantar keratoderma
values.cd30: LyP: recurrent self-healing papulonodules (1-2 cm) at various stages simultaneously. pcALCL: solitary or grouped firm tumors/nodules that may ulcerate

values.mf: Absent or minimal (B0-B1) in most cases; blood involvement (B2) occurs only in advanced or erythrodermic MF
values.ss: DEFINING FEATURE: B2 criteria required — Sézary cells >1000/mcL OR CD4:CD8 >10 OR CD4+CD7- >40% OR CD4+CD26- >30% PLUS clonal TCR in blood
values.cd30: Absent. No peripheral blood involvement; remains purely cutaneous in both LyP and pcALCL

values.mf: Variable; dermatopathic adenopathy common in advanced stages; N3 (effacement) indicates Stage IVA1
values.ss: Generalized lymphadenopathy characteristic; lymph node effacement by Sézary cells common
values.cd30: Absent by definition (primary cutaneous). Regional nodal spread in pcALCL is uncommon (<5%) and does not worsen prognosis

values.mf: Epidermotropic atypical lymphocyte infiltrate; Pautrier microabscesses (10-30%); band-like dermal infiltrate; cerebriform nucleus
values.ss: Epidermotropism often absent or subtle; monotonous dermal infiltrate of large cerebriform Sézary cells; identical clone in skin and blood
values.cd30: LyP type A: large atypical CD30+ cells with Reed-Sternberg-like morphology, inflammatory background. pcALCL: sheets of large pleomorphic CD30+ cells with few admixed inflammatory cells

values.mf: CD3+, CD4+, CD8- (most cases); CD7 loss common; CD26 loss; CD30 variable (positive in large-cell transformation)
values.ss: CD3+, CD4+, CD7- (loss), CD26- (loss); CD56- distinguishes from NK-cell lymphoma; clonal TCR-gamma rearrangement
values.cd30: CD30+ strongly and uniformly (>75% of large cells in pcALCL; variable in LyP subtypes); ALK negative (distinguishes pcALCL from systemic ALCL); CD3+, CD4+ usually

values.mf: Stage IA: ~95-100% (near-normal). Stage IB: ~85%. Stage IIB: ~50-60%. Stage IV: ~20%
values.ss: Approximately 25-35% at 5 years; median OS 2-4 years; prognosis worse than erythrodermic MF alone
values.cd30: LyP: near-normal (5-yr OS >95%); risk of secondary lymphoma ~15%. pcALCL solitary: 5-yr OS >85%. Multifocal pcALCL: ~80%

values.mf: Early (IA-IB): Skin-directed therapy (topical steroids, NB-UVB, PUVA, topical mechlorethamine). Advanced (IIB+): add systemic agents (mogamulizumab, brentuximab if CD30+, bexarotene)
values.ss: Extracorporeal photopheresis (ECP) ± IFN-alpha or bexarotene; mogamulizumab (FDA-approved, Phase III superiority vs vorinostat); ECP combination preferred by most centers
values.cd30: LyP: observation (self-healing); methotrexate low-dose for symptomatic/numerous lesions. pcALCL solitary: excision or local radiation (4-40 Gy). pcALCL multifocal: brentuximab vedotin or methotrexate
